tone_statements.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, Eighteenth edition. Dallas, Texas: SIL International. Online version, entry 'Raute' [rau], 'Typology' field (archived 2015-02-27 at web.archive.org).
tone_statements.quote: It has SOV syntax; it is postpositional; has noun head final; no noun classes or gender; content q-word in situ; clause constituents indicated by case-marking; verbal affixation marks person and number; ergativity; both tense and aspect; non-tonal; 35 consonants and 7 vowel phonemes
tone_statements.locator: Ethnologue entry Raute [rau], 'Language typology' field; as quoted verbatim in Bandhu, Pathak & Rai 2015, A sociolinguistic survey of Raute, sec. 1.0 'Background', p. 1
tone_statements.summary: Database statement: Raute is non-tonal (35 consonants, 7 vowels); no first-hand published analysis of Raute tone exists beyond Fortier & Rastogi's 2004 impressionistic note of word-final falling pitch on long vowels.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for raut1239 (16 entries incl. Tolange 2025 Raute Lexicon Ms., Rastogi & Fortier 2005 Indian Linguistics 66:105-115, Luintel 1993, Shrestha & Singh 1987, Bista 1972).
sources.note: Bibliography only; no phonology-typed reference exists for Raute; the single grammar sketch is Khadka 2006.

sources.citation: Bandhu, Chura Mani, Lekhnath Sharma Pathak & Tara Mani Rai. 2015. A sociolinguistic survey of Raute: A Tibeto-Burman language. Report to Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 145 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 1.0 (p. 1) repeats the Ethnologue typology line: '.. ergativity; both tense and aspect; non-tonal; 35 consonants and 7 vowel phonemes'. Sec. 1.4 and references state the only linguistic work on Raute is Fortier & Rastogi 2004 plus Khadka 2006 (MA sketch grammar and NFDIN documentation report of Boto Boli). Annex wordlists in IPA without stress marks.

sources.citation: Fortier, Jana & Kavita Rastogi. 2004. Sister languages? Comparative phonology of two Himalayan languages. Nepalese Linguistics 21: 42-52.
sources.note: 'Phonological impressions' (p. 44): 19 consonant phonemes for Khaamci; feature list includes '4) Khaamci has long geminate vowels with falling tones in word final position. 5) Women speakers used noticeable creaky tones.' Consonants only (vowels explicitly excluded); no statement on stress/accent placement.

sources.citation: Luintel, Yubaraj. 2055 VS [1998]. Bhramanshil Raute: ek samajshastriya adhyayan [The nomadic Raute: a sociological study]. Kathmandu: Nepal Rajakiya Pragya-Pratisthan. (Nepali)
sources.note: 'Khamci bhasha' section (p. 66f): sociolinguistic remarks, impressionistic notes (r->D, s->h substitutions when speaking Nepali; native numerals 1-6), appendix wordlist; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bista, Dor Bahadur. 1976. Encounter with the Raute: the last hunting nomads of Nepal. Kailash 4(4): 317-327.
sources.note: Ethnography plus Swadesh-100 wordlist (Table I, analysed with Austin Hale); no phonological remarks; silent.

sources.citation: Reinhard, Johan. 1974. The Raute: notes on a nomadic hunting and gathering tribe of Nepal. Kailash 2(4): 233-271.
sources.note: Ethnography; 'History and language' section is classificatory (TB, close only to Raji); no phonology; silent on stress.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only grammatical description of Raute (Glottolog's sole grammar sketch; LinSuN 2015 calls it the only linguistic work besides Fortier & Rastogi). TU sketch grammars have a phonology chapter that normally states whether stress is predictable; likely source of Ethnologue's '35 C, 7 V, non-tonal'. Glottolog/hh holds a scan but it is not in the TU Central Library DSpace.
